arxiv-2103-01529.description: Abstract . We investigate the behaviour of flux-driven flow through a single-phase fluid domain coupled to a biphasic poroelastic domain. The fluid domain consists of an incompressible Newtonian viscous fluid while the poroelastic domain consists of a linearly elastic solid filled with the same viscous fluid. arxiv-2111-04804.title: Approximating Fair Clustering with Cascaded Norm Objectives
arxiv-2111-04804.creator: Eden Chlamtáč, Yury Makarychev, Ali Vakilian
arxiv-2111-04804.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Eden Chlamtáč, Yury Makarychev, Ali Vakilian. We introduce the ( p , q ) (p,q) -Fair Clustering problem. In this problem, we are given a set of points P P and a collection of different weight functions W W . We would like to find a clustering which minimizes the ℓ q \ell_{q} -norm of the vector over W W of the ℓ p \ell_{p} -norms of the weighted distances of points in P P from the centers.

arxiv-2305-11920.title: Megahertz X-ray multi-projection imaging
arxiv-2305-11920.creator: Pablo Villanueva-Perez, Valerio Bellucci, Yuhe Zhang, Šarlota Birnšteinová, Rita Graceffa, Luigi Adriano, Eleni Myrto Asimakopoulou, Ilia Petrov, Zisheng Yao, Marco Romagnoni, Andrea Mazzolari, Romain Letrun, Chan Kim, Jayanath C. P. Koliyadu, Carsten Deiter, Richard Bean, Gabriele Giovanetti, Luca
arxiv-2305-11920.description: Abstract X-ray time-resolved tomography is one of the most popular X-ray techniques to probe dynamics in three dimensions (3D). Recent developments in time-resolved tomography opened the possibility of recording kilohertz-rate 3D movies. However, tomography requires rotating the sample with respect to the X-ray beam, which prevents characterization of faster structural dynamics.

arxiv-2306-09870.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Power Dominating Set
arxiv-2306-09870.creator: Thomas Bläsius, Max Göttlicher
arxiv-2306-09870.description: Abstract The problem Power Dominating Set ( PDS ) is motivated by the placement of phasor measurement units to monitor electrical networks. It asks for a minimum set of vertices in a graph that observes all remaining vertices by exhaustively applying two observation rules. Our contribution is twofold.

arxiv-2306-12333.title: Autonomous Navigation with Convergence Guarantees in Complex Dynamic Environments
arxiv-2306-12333.creator: Albin Dahlin, Yiannis Karayiannidis
arxiv-2306-12333.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Albin Dahlin, Yiannis Karayiannidis. This article addresses the obstacle avoidance problem for setpoint stabilization and path-following tasks in complex dynamic 2D environments that go beyond conventional scenes with isolated convex obstacles. A combined motion planner and controller is proposed for setpoint stabilization that integrates the favorable convergence characteristics of closed-form motion planning techniques with the intuitive representation of system constraints through Model Predictive Control (MPC).

arxiv-2504-00051.title: The Cursive Transformer
arxiv-2504-00051.creator: Sam Greydanus, Zachary Wimpee
arxiv-2504-00051.description: Abstract Transformers trained on tokenized text, audio, and images can generate high-quality autoregressive samples. But handwriting data, represented as sequences of pen coordinates, remains underexplored. We introduce a novel tokenization scheme that converts pen stroke offsets to polar coordinates, discretizes them into bins, and then turns them into sequences of tokens with which to train a standard GPT model.

arxiv-2510-13580.title: Sparse Subnetwork Enhancement for Underrepresented Languages in Large Language Models
arxiv-2510-13580.creator: Daniil Gurgurov Josef van Genabith Simon Ostermann
arxiv-2510-13580.description: Abstract Large language models exhibit uneven performance across languages, with substantial gaps between high- and low-resource languages. We present a framework for enhancing monolingual capabilities of LLMs in underrepresented languages while preserving their general-purpose performance through targeted fine-tuning of language-specific subnetworks.

pmc-10531772.title: The Cytotoxic Effect of Septic Plasma on Healthy RBCs: Is Eryptosis a New Mechanism for Sepsis?
pmc-10531772.creator: Matteo Marcello, Grazia Maria Virzì, Davide Marturano, Massimo de Cal, Nicola Marchionna, Luca Sgarabotto, Silvia De Rosa, Claudio Ronco, Monica Zanella, Dumitru Constantin-Teodosiu
pmc-10531772.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening multiple-organ dysfunction induced by infection and is one of the leading causes of mortality and critical illness worldwide. The pathogenesis of sepsis involves the alteration of several biochemical pathways such as immune response, coagulation, dysfunction of endothelium and tissue damage through cellular death and/or apoptosis.

pmc-11429403.title: Occurrence, Source Apportionment, and Risk Assessment of Antibiotics in Mangrove Sediments from the Lianzhou Bay, China
pmc-11429403.creator: Pengfei Sun, Yongyu Tan, Zuhao Zhu, Tinglong Yang, Shalini Thevarajan, Li Zhang
pmc-11429403.description: In recent years, the widespread application of antibiotics has raised global concerns, posing a severe threat to ecological health. In this study, the occurrence, source, and ecological risks of 39 antibiotics belonging to 5 classes in mangrove sediments from Lianzhou Bay, China, were assessed. The total concentrations of the antibiotics (∑39 antibiotics) ranged from 65.45 to 202.

pmc-11653691.title: Pathogenic spectrum of infective endocarditis and analysis of prognostic risk factors following surgical treatment in a tertiary hospital in China
pmc-11653691.creator: Suiqing Huang, Jiantao Chen, Tongxin Chu, Li Luo, Quan Liu, Kangni Feng, Zeyu Li, Jian Hou, Zhongkai Wu
pmc-11653691.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to summarize the pathogenic spectrum of infective endocarditis (IE) and analyze the risk factors for poor prognosis in surgical patients in a tertiary hospital in China.MethodsWe retrospectively included patients diagnosed with IE between January 2013 and January 2022.

pmc-12459335.title: Strategic value-directed remembering in younger and older adults
pmc-12459335.creator: Kara M. Hoover, Dillon H. Murphy, Barbara J. Knowlton, Alan D. Castel
pmc-12459335.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To examine potential age-related differences in controlled memory processes, we investigated whether strategic value-based processes can override the influence of information memorability and enhance memory performance for important information in younger and older adults. In three experiments, we manipulated the memorability (using word length, concreteness, and frequency in Experiments 1 and 2 and presentation time in Experiment 3) and the value of words to investigate the influence of item properties versus strategic processes on value-directed remembering in younger and older adults.

pmc-12617036.title: Histological and Gene Expression Analyses of the Arm and Finger Macroglands of Two Hyloxalus Frogs (Dendrobatidae)
pmc-12617036.creator: Diana Abondano Almeida, Marvin Anganoy‐Criollo, Taran Grant, Sofiia Klimovych, Lisa M Schulte
pmc-12617036.description: Chemical communication during courtship is well documented in salamanders and newts, but its role in frogs is less understood. In some Neotropical poison frogs, males exhibit specialised mucous glands (SMGs) in the hand integument that express high levels of sodefrin precursor‐like factors (SPFs), an amphibian pheromone.

pmc-12742662.title: Trueness of Intraoral Scanners for Edentulous Mandibular Arches With and Without Landmarks
pmc-12742662.creator: Filip Rebelo Dessborn, Michael Braian
pmc-12742662.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe purpose of this in vitro study was to evaluate the trueness of three intraoral scanners (IOS) and to assess the impact of geometrical landmarks on the digitization of edentulous mandibular complete-arch casts using a standardized scanning protocol.Material and MethodsA 3D-printed edentulous mandibular cast with five cylindrical landmarks was scanned using three IOS systems (Medit i700, Primescan AC and Trios 5) under two conditions: with and without geometrical landmarks (GL/NG). Each scanner performed 15 scans per condition.

pmc-12997033.title: A systematic evaluation of uncertainty quantification techniques in deep learning: a case study in photoplethysmography signal analysis
pmc-12997033.creator: Ciaran Bench, Oskar Pfeffer, Vivek Desai, Mohammad Moulaeifard, Loic Coquelin, Peter H Charlton, Nils Strodthoff, Nando Hegemann, Philip J Aston, Andrew Thompson
pmc-12997033.description: In principle, deep learning models trained on medical time-series, including wearable photoplethysmography sensor data, can provide a means to continuously monitor physiological parameters outside of clinical settings. However, there is considerable risk of poor performance when deployed in practical measurement scenarios leading to negative patient outcomes.

pmc-13209979.title: Comparison of the effect of eight weeks of Rhythmic aerobic training and CX-WORX on cholesterol transport and inflammatory factors in obese women
pmc-13209979.creator: Samira Sabetrasekh, Allahyar Arabmomeni, Jamshid Banaei Borojeni
pmc-13209979.description: BACKGROUND:Obesity is associated with a wide range of complications and an increased risk of premature occurrence of physical problems, mental disorders, and some diseases. Doing sports activities along with other treatment strategies can be an effective solution to overcome this problem.

pmc-13244262.title: A Multicenter, Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled, Randomized Clinical Trial of Oral Anticoagulation in Systemic Sclerosis‐Related Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension—Results From the SPHInX Study
pmc-13244262.creator: Mandana Nikpour, Alicia Calderone, Susanna M. Proudman, Dylan Hansen, Eli Gabbay, Nathan Dwyer, Gregory Keir, Vivek Thakkar, Peter K. K. Wong, Anne Keogh, Andrew Burns, David Prior, Harshal Nandurkar, David S. Celermajer, Joanne Sahhar, Rachelle Buchbinder, Wendy Stevens
pmc-13244262.description: The SPHInX study is the first‐ever randomized controlled trial (RCT) seeking to inform an area of equipoise regarding the efficacy of oral anticoagulation as adjunct therapy in systemic sclerosis‐related pulmonary arterial hypertension (SSc‐PAH). The SPHInX study was an Australian multicenter, double‐blind Phase III RCT of 1:1 oral apixaban 2.
